findings.automaticCopying: Explicit provider-to-EventKit mirror copies ARE present, including fallback to calDAV/default source. Do not promise data only stays at original provider. Separate provider maps do not establish a general Google-to-Microsoft or reverse bridge.
findings.busyMasking: No automatic cross-provider anonymous busy-block feature found in the inspected sync/transfer paths or focused Calendar Swift search for busy/freeBusy/mask. Bounded negative evidence, not exhaustive absence proof.
findings.manualMoves: Cross-backend explicit move code exists; do not conflate with automatic mirror/sync or market it as harmless copying.
findings.permissions: Local and EventKit edit restrictions exist, but provider list models omit accessRole/canEdit. Do not promise all displayed provider calendars editable or server ACL enforcement reflected perfectly in UI.
findings.microsoft: Common Microsoft authority and Graph delegated scopes observed. No generic on-premises Exchange authentication recipe or verified complete shared/delegated mailbox support.
findings.storageConcern: Destination fallback deserves owner/runtime review for personal/work data boundaries. No device-specific actual destination observed.

suggestedSyncGuideClarification: Seeing calendars together does not itself merge their accounts. However, the app’s Google and Microsoft connections create calendar copies through the iPhone calendar system for synchronization. The calendar source used for those copies can depend on the device’s available sources, so do not assume that data exists only at the original provider. Keep the original provider, the displayed calendar copy and any deliberate event move distinct when checking duplicates or changes.
